福爾摩沙小導遊臺南 Tainan・東區

府東創意森林（原台南州立農事試驗場宿舍群）The Fudong Creative Forest

「工業日本，農業台灣」—— 這是殖民時代的口號。這片幽靜的日式宿舍群，是台南州立農事試驗場科學家們的家。試驗場設立於 1923 年，當時日本的政策把台灣定位為帝國的糧倉。這項政策也留下嘉南大圳與桃園大圳，至今仍支撐台灣農業。宿舍群現存五棟：場長宿舍、兩棟丙種與兩棟丁種判任官舍。用庭院判斷職等：場長宿舍的緣廊最深、老樹最大。獲邀入內時記得脫鞋，感受腳下的榻榻米。2004 年，宿舍群公告為市定古蹟。如今由文化業者經營，合稱「府東創意森林」—— 一座咖啡與文創的森林。

Industrial Japan, Agricultural Taiwan. That was the colonial slogan. This quiet cluster of Japanese dormitories was the home of the scientists who ran the Tainan Prefectural Agricultural Experiment Station. The station was founded in 1923, when Japan's policy cast Taiwan as the food supplier of the empire. The same policy also built the great Chianan and Taoyuan irrigation canals. They still support Taiwanese agriculture today. Five dormitory buildings survive: the station chief's residence, two Type C houses, and two Type D houses. Rank the houses by their gardens. The station chief's residence has the deepest veranda and the biggest trees. Take off your shoes where invited, and feel tatami underfoot. In 2004, the dormitory complex was declared a municipal heritage site. Today, cultural operators run the houses as the Fudong Creative Forest, a forest of cafes and culture.

一分鐘看懂

One-minute intro

為什麼值得來

Why it matters & history

府東創意森林是台南州立農事試驗場留下的日式宿舍群。它見證日治時期「農業台灣」的政策與嘉南大圳的年代；如今老屋、老樹與榻榻米，變成咖啡與文創的森林。

The Fudong Creative Forest is a group of Japanese-era houses built for the scientists of the Tainan agricultural research station. Today the old houses, old trees and tatami rooms hold cafes and craft shops.

  1. 1923台南州立農事試驗場設立，科學家住進這片宿舍。The Tainan agricultural research station is set up, and its scientists move into these houses.
  2. 日治時期 Japanese era「工業日本，農業台灣」政策下，也興建了嘉南大圳。Under the policy of farming Taiwan, the Chianan Canal is also built.
  3. 2004現存五棟宿舍公告為市定古蹟。The five remaining houses become a city monument.
  4. 今天 Today由文化業者經營，合稱府東創意森林。Cultural businesses run them together as the Fudong Creative Forest.

認識景點

About the place

農事試驗場：科學家研究農業的地方。這座設立於 1923 年。 科學家：這些宿舍是經營試驗場的科學家們的家。 口號：一句簡短的口號。殖民口號是「工業日本，農業台灣」。 糧倉、糧食供應地：日本的政策把台灣定位為帝國的糧倉。

agricultural experiment station: A place where scientists study farming. This one was founded in 1923. scientist: The dormitories were the homes of the scientists who ran the station. slogan: A short saying. The colonial slogan was Industrial Japan, Agricultural Taiwan. food supplier: Japan's policy cast Taiwan as the food supplier of the empire.

灌溉水圳：為農田引水的人工水道。嘉南大圳與桃園大圳至今仍支撐農業。 宿舍群：一群員工宿舍。這裡現存五棟。 場長宿舍：最大的一棟，緣廊最深、老樹最大。 判任官舍：官員的宿舍。現存兩棟丙種、兩棟丁種判任官舍。

irrigation canal: A man-made waterway for farms. The Chianan and Taoyuan canals still support farming today. dormitory complex: A group of houses for workers. Five dormitory buildings survive here. the station chief's residence: The biggest house, with the deepest veranda and the biggest trees. official house: A house for officials. Two Type C and two Type D official houses survive.

緣廊：沿著房屋的木造走廊。在緣廊歇歇腳。 榻榻米：日式地墊。脫鞋感受腳下的榻榻米。 古蹟：受保護的歷史場所。宿舍群 2004 年成為市定古蹟。 文化業者：經營文化場所的業者。他們合稱「府東創意森林」。

veranda: A wooden porch along a house. Rest your feet among the wooden verandas. tatami: A Japanese floor mat. Take off your shoes and feel tatami underfoot. heritage site: A protected historic place. The complex became a municipal heritage site in 2004. cultural operator: A group that runs a cultural place. Cultural operators run the houses as the Fudong Creative Forest.

實景照片

Photos on site

老樹圍繞的宿舍群 Houses among old trees

從路口看過去，高大的老樹和整齊的綠籬圍著一片日式宿舍，在大樓之間像一座小森林。

From the street corner, tall old trees and neat hedges surround a group of Japanese-era houses, like a small forest among the tall buildings.

樹林裡的日式宿舍 A wooden house in the trees

綠樹圍繞的日式木造宿舍，是日治時期臺南州立農事試驗場的宿舍群之一。看看灰色的屋瓦、木板牆，還有窗戶上方小小的屋簷。

Among the trees stands a Japanese-style wooden house. It is one of the dormitories of the old agricultural experiment station. Look at the grey roof tiles, the wooden walls, and the little roofs over the windows.

有緣側的宿舍 A house with a veranda

這棟宿舍前面有長長的緣側（木造走廊），屋頂鋪著日式黑瓦。依現場解說牌，宿舍群共有五棟：一棟場長宿舍、兩棟丙種和兩棟丁種官舍；丙種和丁種都是兩戶並排的雙併屋。

This house has a long wooden veranda, and its roof is covered with dark Japanese tiles. The sign here says there are five houses: one for the station director, and four smaller ones, each shared by two families.

雨淋板和鬼瓦 Wooden boards and ridge tiles

仔細看木板牆：一片片木板上下疊著，叫做「雨淋板」，雨水會順著板子往下流，不會滲進牆裡。屋脊尾端翹起的裝飾瓦叫「鬼瓦」，是日式屋頂的特色。

Look closely at the walls. The boards overlap from top to bottom, so rain runs down the outside instead of soaking in. The decorated tile at the end of the roof ridge is called an onigawara, a feature of Japanese roofs.

老屋變文創 Old houses, new shops

老宿舍現在由文化業者經營，門口掛上布簾和招牌，變成咖啡店和文創小店，合稱「府東創意森林」。

Today cultural businesses run the old houses. Cloth curtains and signs hang at the doors, and the houses hold cafes and craft shops, together called the Fudong Creative Forest.

宿舍之間的草地 The lawn between the houses

宿舍之間是開闊的草地和石板步道，可以慢慢散步，從不同角度看老屋的屋頂和緣側。

Open lawns and stone paths lie between the houses. Take a slow walk and look at the roofs and verandas from different sides.

綠籬與老石牆 Hedge and old stone wall

綠籬後面是一道老石牆，牆內大樹下就是宿舍。依解說牌，場長宿舍是獨門獨院的房子，和其他宿舍分開。

Behind the hedge runs an old stone wall, with a house under the big trees inside. The sign says the director's house stood alone in its own yard, apart from the others.
